entries.title: Return to Tsugaru
entries.author: 太宰 治
entries.sourceName: Japan Foundation — Japanese Book News 75, pp. 12–13
entries.text: In 1944, Osamu Dazai travels back to Tsugaru, the northern Japanese region where he grew up. A commission to describe his birthplace becomes a more personal investigation of memory, belonging and his relationships with people from his past. The narrative combines observations of the region with encounters, recollections and self-questioning. Return to Tsugaru offers a literary journey through a familiar landscape made strange by absence, bringing the author’s personality into the foreground of the account.
entries.identityNotes: Japan Foundation work study pp12–13 supports travel, 1944 setting, structure and personal focus. Kodansha original translation title confirmed by its publisher advertisement in Journal of Asian Studies47/1; selected1985ISBN9780870116865 retained. Literary narrative, not presented as objective autobiography or practical current travel advice.

entries.title: Welcome to Dead House
entries.author: Robert Lawrence Stine
entries.text: Amanda and Josh move with their parents to an old house in the unfamiliar town of Dark Falls. The house feels wrong, and the surrounding community offers little reassurance, but the adults expect the children to settle in and make friends. Their new acquaintances soon make that advice seem dangerous. R. L. Stine’s Goosebumps story turns the unease of moving home into a mystery about a town whose welcome hides a frightening intention.
entries.identityNotes: Official publisher synopsis for the original story; exact selected ScholasticISBN9780545086042, author Robert Lawrence Stine. No television adaptation or edition-exclusive additions claimed.
